motion.name: ease-dispatch

motion.name: duration-transfer
motion.purpose: View-transition group for a nudge. The root snapshot does not crossfade, and the arrival fallback does not also run.

motion.name: duration-arrival
motion.purpose: Fallback when view transitions are unavailable. Opacity and a rise from -0.35rem, with no blur. None when the shared transition runs or reduced motion is requested.

motion.name: duration-status
motion.purpose: Moss status line fades in after a state change. Skipped when reduced motion is requested.

motion.name: duration-composer-open
motion.purpose: Open a loop expands. Closing takes 180ms on the dispatch curve.

motion.name: duration-mark
motion.purpose: The plus on Open a loop turns 45 degrees.

motion.name: duration-route
motion.purpose: Root crossfade between routes. The phone tab bar stays still.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active button over 150ms on the dispatch curve. Reduced motion keeps the scale at 1.

narrative.overview:
Looops is a cool-mist ledger for work other people still hold. Forest ink does the reading, one dispatch green marks the next move, and pale seams separate the lines. Density stays low, and a wait never changes color to manufacture urgency.

Every route uses the same frame. From the wide breakpoint a sticky masthead sits beside a flush ledger; below that, the masthead stacks and the rows run the width of the page. Today’s masthead is the date. Loops, a loop, and a reply use a title. Archive state is a ruled group, never a badge. History is a quiet date column. A reply is a ruled decision, and its action stays on the far edge when the row stacks.

A dispatched line transfers into Nudged today; the rest of the page stays still. When reduced motion is requested, the line changes place with no transfer and no arrival motion. On the phone, a sticky back bar appears only on a loop and a reply. The bottom tabs are the two places, Today and Loops, and their focus ring sits inside the bar.
keyCharacteristics: Cool mist ground, forest ink, and one dispatch green for the decisive fill
Timeless Sans throughout: an oversized tabular date, or a tight title masthead
Flush ruled rows, square frames, and no status badges
One filled action at the terminal edge, even when the row stacks
A shared colored wordmark, an inset focus ring on phone chrome, and a dispatch the reduced-motion setting removes

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Dispatch green is the date numeral, text selection, the caret, the focus ring, and the single decisive fill on a row or decision. It is not a status color.

rules.name: The Quiet Wait Rule
rules.body: Waiting age stays moss and tabular. Brick marks an invalid field or a backup that cannot be read, never a wait.

rules.name: The Mark Rule
rules.body: Loop sage is the third stroke of the mark. It is not a fill for buttons, rows, or status.

rules.name: The Grotesk Rule
rules.body: Timeless Sans is the only face, from the date numeral through the title, the row, and the controls.

rules.name: The Masthead Rule
rules.body: From 64rem a sticky masthead sits beside the ledger, offset 2.5rem from the top. Today carries the date; the other routes carry a title. Below that, the masthead stacks and the rows run edge to edge.

rules.name: The Terminal Edge Rule
rules.body: The decisive action is the last control and sits on the far edge, including when the row stacks. Quiet and outline actions stay unfilled beside it.

rules.name: The Archive Rule
rules.body: Derived state is a ruled group heading and a moss count. A line does not wear a badge.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: Surfaces cast no shadow. Separation comes from rule weight and from paper tone on hover and on entry forms.

rules.name: The Square Frame Rule
rules.body: Rows, the phone nav, the back bar, and entry forms are square. Open a loop, the next person, and handoff are ledger paper inside a 1px deep-forest stroke. The backup band is square paper under a quiet rule. Buttons use the 6px control radius; fields use the wider field radius.

rules.name: The Still Page Rule
rules.body: When a line is dispatched, the root view transition does not crossfade. Only the named line moves, and reduced motion removes even that. A route change is separate: the root crossfades over 200ms on `cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`, while the phone tab bar stays still.

rules.name: The Inset Chrome Rule
rules.body: Phone tabs and the back bar take a 2px dispatch outline inset by 2px. Buttons and text links keep that outline offset 2px outside.

dos: Do set the page on cool mist, read it in forest ink, and keep dispatch green to the decisive fill, the numeral, selection, the caret, and focus.
Do set follow-ups and the people in a loop as flush ruled rows, history as a quiet date column, and the archive as ruled groups with a moss count and no badge on the line.
Do keep the one filled action at the terminal edge, including when the row stacks.
Do keep entry forms square — ledger paper inside a 1px deep-forest stroke — and the backup band square paper under a quiet rule.
Do use the shared wordmark. On the phone, detail and reply get a sticky back bar; tabs and that bar take an inset 2px dispatch outline.
Do transfer a dispatched line over 280ms on `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)`, and skip that transfer when reduced motion is requested.
donts: Don't restyle a follow-up, a person in the loop, or a routing decision as a stacked card, a stat tile, or a dashboard widget.
Don't give Defer, Close, and Nudge the same fill, and don't turn archive state into a badge.
Don't set display type in a serif, and don't paint with the warm parchment palette or the unused dark-theme tokens.
Don't color a wait as overdue, and don't add streaks or guilt counts.
Don't put a drop shadow on a row, a form, a tab, or a button.
Don't crossfade the whole page when a line is dispatched.
